findings.title: Integer division truncates before multiplying by 100
findings.description: `spent // b["limit_cents"] * 100` performs integer division first, so pct is 0 for any spend below 100% of the limit (e.g. spent=8000, limit=10000 gives pct=0 instead of 80). This makes the alert essentially only fire once spend has reached at least the full budget (>=100%, since anything below rounds to 0), defeating the purpose of an early warning at 80%. Should be `spent * 100 // limit_cents` or use float division.

findings.title: Threshold comparison excludes the boundary
findings.description: The description says alerts should fire for categories that have 'reached' the threshold percentage, implying >=, but the code uses `pct > threshold_pct`, so a category exactly at 80% (or exactly at 100%, i.e. exactly over budget) is not flagged.

findings.title: Division by zero when budget limit is 0
findings.description: If a budget row has `limit_cents == 0`, computing `spent // b["limit_cents"]` raises ZeroDivisionError, crashing the report instead of handling the edge case (e.g. treating any spend as immediately over budget).

findings.title: No tests for budget_alerts
findings.description: The PR adds a new public function `budget_alerts` with threshold logic, percentage math, and a configurable parameter, but no tests are included to verify correct behavior, the default threshold, custom thresholds, or edge cases like zero-limit budgets or spend exactly at the threshold.
